extraction_scope: Worker-6 bounded mechanism adjudication from source-reviewed paper prose; no direct molecular mechanism is promoted from this paper alone.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: The Cha analogues show strong antibacterial phenotype evidence against Gram-positive bacteria in primary MIC assays.
mechanism_claims.limitations: MIC phenotype supports antimicrobial activity but does not identify a new direct molecular target in this paper.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: The paper interprets enhanced activity of hydrophobic Cha substitutions as consistent with stronger interactions between clovibactin analogues and bacterial membranes.
mechanism_claims.limitations: This is author interpretation tied to prior clovibactin work and MIC trends, not a direct binding or membrane-disruption assay in this paper.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: Hemolysis/cytotoxicity trends support a caution that increased hydrophobicity also increases mammalian-cell interaction liability.
mechanism_claims.limitations: This bounds selectivity/toxicity interpretation and is not classified as a direct antimicrobial mechanism.

caution_findings.note: No direct target-binding, lipid-II binding, or membrane permeabilization assay is newly performed in this paper; mechanism claims remain phenotype/inference/context only.
